proven: The same persistent browser profile downloaded content, was closed, and was relaunched offline.
The relaunched offline page required an explicit resume, then accepted local seek and pause.
While that browser remained offline, a separate authenticated API context advanced the authoritative server session revision.
The same browser profile reconnected, resolved the conflict by keeping device state, and the server logical queue retained its duplicate and Wait entries.
continuity_scope.boundary: The offline downloaded queue/checkpoint and the authoritative server logical queue are distinct state representations. The run proves their continuous same-profile reconnect interaction and final server-queue preservation; it does not assert byte-for-byte equality between those representations.
continuity_scope.offline_boundary: The browser network was disabled; the fixture server remained available only to the separate context that deliberately created the concurrent revision. This is not a server-process-outage proof.

unproven: physical-device playback, route changes, receiver behavior, and energy behavior
